sentences.text: You slam the fire exit and drag four pallets of cat litter against it.
Then you lock every door and snap your own key off in the staff entrance.
Now nobody can get in.
You tell yourself that is the same as nobody being inside.
The footprints dry up by the bakery.
You search every aisle with a flashlight from aisle 9.
Nothing.
Emergency lights are built to last two hours, long enough for everyone to leave.
Nobody planned for somebody staying.
When they die, you learn something about supermarkets.
They have no windows.
With the shutter down, you have built yourself a cave.
Problem two: the rot.
Without power, a fridge keeps food safe for five hours.
A full freezer, three days.
After that, you are sealed in with three tons of meat, milk and fish.
But there is a walk-in freezer, a steel room with a rubber seal.
It keeps the warm air out, and everything else in.
You spend nine hours and one cart filling it.
You keep the bread and the fruit.
Then you tape the seams and write on the door: do not open.
Ever.
On the second morning, something is wrong.
The tins you stacked in aisle 5 have been rebuilt into a pyramid.
You did not build a pyramid.
You check the cameras.
They have no power.
You check the locks.
Every one is still shut.
Somebody is living in this building with you.
On the fourth morning, you climb onto the roof.
Three nights ago, the parking lot was empty.
Now there are 150 people standing in it, all facing the doors.
They are not hunting you.
They are waiting for the store to open.
